candidates.tagline: Built in August. Went nowhere. Blocked an ambulance. Gone by October.
candidates.story: In August 2026, Boston installed a roughly 100-foot protected bike lane on O'Connor Way in South Boston that didn't connect to any other cycling infrastructure; the lane sat in unpaved gravel, removed accessible parking spots for a senior housing building, and was torn out by October after ambulances couldn't navigate past it — with the city still refusing to disclose what either the construction or the demolition cost.
candidates.why_funny: The city built infrastructure specifically for people trying to get somewhere, that literally went nowhere, then paid again to remove it, and won't say what either trip cost.
candidates.alt: New concrete curb barriers forming a short bike lane on O'Connor Way in South Boston, flanked entirely by loose gravel where pavement should be, clearly unfinished and unconnected to any other cycling infrastructure

candidates.tagline: JLo's $150 crystal lip balm is the same $19 formula with Swarovski on the tin.
candidates.story: On November 5, 2026, JLo Beauty released Beso Bling — three limited-edition lip balms encrusted with Swarovski crystals, each priced at $150 (or $225 for the set), compared to the $19 Beso Balm they're based on — accompanied by a surreal AI-generated promo video labeled 'AI content' that showed cherries rolling through subway cars and crystal-covered hummingbirds, prompting critics to call it 'the dumbest product launch in history.'
candidates.why_funny: JLo Beauty's answer to 'how do we innovate our lip balm?' was: apply Swarovski crystals to the same formula and charge eight times as much, then hire an AI to write the ad because apparently the concept required no human creativity either.
candidates.alt: Jennifer Lopez posing in a composite image flanked by two oversized pink Beso Bling lip balm containers decorated with large Swarovski crystals — JLo Beauty's $150 limited-edition version of their $19 original lip balm
